name: Jashen
overview: Jashen was a male warrior known primarily as the son of Eliahba and recognized as the twenty-third member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture, and there are no additional notes about his life or character. His mention is brief but places him among David's celebrated warriors.
namesAndTitles: The name Jashen is a proper name that possibly means "asleep," though this is not definitively established. He is also referred to as Hashem, meaning "the name," in another biblical passage. Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jashen was the son of Eliahba. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jashen's significance lies in his inclusion among David's thirty mighty men, a distinguished group of warriors who played a key role in establishing and defending David's kingdom. Being the twenty-third listed highlights his recognized valor and contribution within this elite band. Although not much detail is provided about his individual exploits, his mention affirms the collective strength and loyalty that supported David's reign.
